questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The best romantic films of the 1950s
How actors learn to dance in musicals
Why black-and-white films are still popular
How intimate scenes are planned and filmed safely
questions.why: They discuss filming intimate scenes and the job of the intimacy coordinator.

questions.q: Why does Georgina tease Neil early in the programme?
options: Because he doesn't like romantic films
Because he forgot the name of a film
Because the old films he mentions show his age
Because he has never seen Titanic
questions.why: After he mentions classic films from 1942 and 1951, she says 'You're really showing your age, Neil!'

questions.q: According to Neil, why can romantic scenes in films cause problems?
options: Because audiences usually find them boring and too slow
Because the actors are only pretending to be intimate
Because they are too expensive and take days to film
Because they make films too long for cinemas to show
questions.why: Neil says actors are just pretending to be intimate, and this can lead to problems.

options: She helps plan and film intimate scenes
She writes romantic dramas for BBC television
She is the director of 'Normal People'
She teaches actors to kiss
questions.why: She is an 'intimacy coordinator' who helps actors and directors plan and film intimate scenes.

questions.q: How does Ita O'Brien define intimacy?
options: Only as sex scenes shown on screen
Only as kissing between two actors
As any scene with two actors in it
From holding hands to simulated sex
questions.why: Her definition goes from a hand hold and a hug right through to simulated sexual content.

questions.q: Why are intimate scenes planned and choreographed beforehand?
options: So that everyone, especially the actors, is comfortable
So that filming finishes more quickly and costs less money
So that the scenes look more like dances in musicals
So that the film has a better chance of winning an Oscar
questions.why: Neil says they are planned so the director, crew and above all the actors are comfortable.

questions.q: How is the UK system different from the US system, according to Ita O'Brien?
options: UK actors sign nothing at all before filming
US actors sign one document for the whole film
UK: one clause for all; US: one per scene
In the US only the director signs a document
questions.why: She says in the US there's a waiver for each intimate scene, but in the UK one clause covers the production.

questions.q: Which way of working does Ita O'Brien prefer?
options: The British way, with one document for the whole film
The US way, agreeing to every single scene
Having no written documents or contracts at all
Letting the director decide everything on the day
questions.why: About the US scene-by-scene waiver, she says 'I actually really like that way of working'.
